carried.old_section: Policy-gradient line / Optimise the policy directly
carried.fact: tau = (s0, a0, r1, s1, ...) trajectory; G(tau) its discounted return
theta changes which trajectories are sampled; dynamics unknown, so the expectation cannot be differentiated directly
Log-derivative trick: grad E[f] = E[f grad log p] because grad p = p grad log p
Trajectory log-probability = policy terms + dynamics terms independent of theta, so dynamics drop out
Theorem: grad J = E[sum_t grad log pi(a_t|s_t) Q_pi(s_t,a_t)] (Sutton et al. 1999, link)
Score function = direction making a_t more likely; Q_pi = expected return after taking it
In words: push up log-probability in proportion to how good; needs only samples and differentiable log-probabilities, never a model
REINFORCE (Williams 1992, link) is the Monte Carlo version using the sampled return
G_t = sum_k gamma^k r_{t+k+1}; rewards before t dropped since an action cannot affect the past
Unbiased but very high variance; when all rewards are positive every sampled action is pushed up, good ones more
Any baseline b(s) independent of the action leaves the gradient unbiased; the proof sum grad pi = grad 1 = 0
b(s) = V_pi(s) turns the weight into the advantage A = Q - V, how much better than average
Variance-minimising constant baseline is a weighted mean of returns, not exactly V; V is close and what practice uses
carried.here: #rd-base (b* formula, Greensmith et al. 2004, rd-bx widget)

carried.fact: Worked example: rewards 1, 2, 6, uniform softmax, V = 3; score e_a - pi; exact gradient (-0.667, -0.333, 1)
Sample action 1 no baseline (0.667, -0.333, -0.333) raises worst action; with baseline (-1.333, 0.667, 0.667)
Sample action 3: (-2, -2, 4) without, (-1, -1, 2) with
Both average to (-0.667, -0.333, 1); total variance 7.56 to 1.56; baseline 3 is also variance-minimising here because all score vectors have the same length
GRPO's group-mean baseline is this idea with V replaced by the mean reward of a group of responses (link RL for LLMs)
carried.note: refined: GRPO also divides by the group std; it is REINFORCE-family, not actor-critic

carried.fact: REINFORCE needs whole episodes and a separate V estimate; actor-critic learns actor and critic V(s;w) at once, critic by TD
TD error delta_t = r + gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t), 0 if terminal; expectation equals A_pi when critic exact
Low variance, biased when critic wrong; return minus V unbiased and high variance: the MC vs TD dial
GAE (Schulman et al. 2015, link) exponentially weighted sum of TD errors, analogous to TD(lambda)
lambda = 0 gives one-step TD error (lowest variance, most bias); lambda = 1 gives return minus V (unbiased, highest variance)
PPO reference settings lambda = 0.95, gamma = 0.99
Worked example gamma = 1: rewards 0, 0, 1; V 0.5, 0.6, 0.8; deltas 0.1, 0.2, 0.2; A0 = 0.1, 0.4705, 0.5
A3C (Mnih et al. 2016, link): many CPU actor-learners, own environment copies, asynchronous gradients to shared weights
Parallel actors decorrelate data like replay while staying on-policy; state-of-the-art Atari on CPU alone
carried.note: made precise: half the training time on a single multi-core CPU, 16 threads

carried.fact: A2C synchronous: wait for all actors, one batched update; OpenAI found it as good as A3C, no evidence asynchrony helps, better GPU use (OpenAI Baselines link)
carried.note: quoted: performs better; cost-effective on single-GPU machines

carried.fact: Modern LLM RL loops have this shape: a batch of rollouts then an update

carried.old_section: TRPO to PPO / Why the step size is dangerous
carried.fact: Gradient valid only near the data-collecting policy; a bad step corrupts the next batch; goal is the largest safe step and several gradient steps per batch

carried.old_section: TRPO to PPO / Why the step size is dangerous
carried.fact: Surrogate built from importance ratio r_t = pi_theta / pi_old; same gradient as PG at theta_old; ratio corrects drift (importance sampling for a stale policy)
TRPO (Schulman et al. 2015, link) maximises the surrogate subject to mean KL(old||new) <= delta
Fisher information matrix as curvature; natural-gradient step by conjugate gradient, then line search
Works but heavy, awkward with shared policy and value networks, hard to scale
carried.here: #rd-trpo (PPO paper quote on dropout and parameter sharing)

carried.fact: PPO (Schulman et al. 2017, link) replaces the constraint with a pessimistic clipped objective optimisable by SGD; L^CLIP formula
clip range epsilon; 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 compared on continuous control, 0.2 best; Atari started at 0.1 and annealed to 0
Good action: flat once r > 1 + eps; bad action: flat once r < 1 - eps; wrong-way ratio never clipped
Worked table eps 0.2: (A +2, r 1.5) 2.4 zero; (A +2, r 0.7) 1.4 active; (A -1, r 0.7) -0.8 zero; (A -1, r 1.5) -1.5 active
TRPO-like stability first-order; several epochs (10 continuous control, 3 Atari)
Full loss has value regression term and usually entropy bonus
Much of practical performance is implementation details such as advantage normalisation and learning-rate annealing
This objective is the core of RLHF with PPO and of GRPO
With continuous actions max_a Q is an optimisation; these methods learn an actor that performs it and keep replay and target networks
DDPG (Lillicrap et al. 2015, link): deterministic actor maximises Q(s, mu(s)) via grad_a Q; critic target r + gamma Q(s', mu(s'; theta-); w-); sample-efficient but brittle
TD3 (Fujimoto et al. 2018, link): overestimation persists in actor-critic; twin critics (clipped double Q), delayed policy updates, target policy smoothing
SAC (Haarnoja et al. 2018, link): stochastic actor, maximum-entropy objective J = sum E[r + alpha H]; H definition; integral for continuous
Even split between two actions has entropy ln 2 = 0.693, worth 0.139 per step at alpha 0.2; deterministic policy earns nothing
Entropy bonus keeps exploration alive, robust across seeds; common off-policy default for continuous control and robotics
Same idea reappears in LLM RL as KL and entropy terms that stop collapse onto a single mode
carried.note: refined: a KL to a reference is not an entropy bonus

carried.fact: REINFORCE: policy, model-free, on-policy, any action space
A2C, A3C: actor-critic, model-free, on-policy, any
TRPO, PPO: actor-critic, model-free, approximately on-policy (ratios), any
DDPG, TD3, SAC: actor-critic, model-free, off-policy replay, continuous

carried.old_section: Trade-offs and when to use which
carried.fact: LLM post-training: PPO with value model or GRPO (link)
"A baseline biases the gradient": state-only baselines do not; action-dependent would
"PPO's clip bounds the ratio": bounds only the incentive; monitor clip fraction and KL
"PPO is on-policy so cannot reuse data": reuses each batch for several epochs
"Off-policy means offline": DQN and SAC interact online and learn from replay
"Entropy bonuses are a hack": in SAC entropy is part of the objective with a principled temperature
